subject.title: feat: clarify publisher state and discovery labels

question: Should ClawHub support `claimState`, `officialState`, and `restrictionState` as a durable official-publisher admin API contract, or keep this work limited to the existing Official presentation facts for now?
rationale: The choice defines identity and trust semantics that downstream tooling may treat as authoritative; code review cannot safely select that product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow and prove the contract
options.body: Require observed-active-user claim derivation and redacted real Convex/API proof, then accept the state vocabulary only if it remains useful to the supported admin contract.

options.title: Land presentation clarification only
options.body: Retain the bounded UI wording changes that use the existing official fact, while deferring the new state object and its policy vocabulary to a sponsored design.

options.title: Defer publisher-state vocabulary
options.body: Leave the current official-publisher response unchanged until claim and restriction policy has an approved broader product design.

recommendation.title: Narrow and prove the contract
recommendation.body: Require observed-active-user claim derivation and redacted real Convex/API proof, then accept the state vocabulary only if it remains useful to the supported admin contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the requested code owner for the affected publisher administration and client-contract surface.
